title: [finding] checklist-select self-test prints a transcribed `17 cases` literal — accurate today, derived by nothing, and the pre-stale form of #15231 / #15291
body:
Measured on `origin/main` = `fbecffe1d` by the #13799 batch-8 census (read-only worktree, installed).

## The reading

`scripts/checklist-select.mjs:159` prints its case count as a **hard-coded literal**:

```js
console.log('✓ checklist-select self-test: 17 cases pass.');
```

The body registers its cases through a block-bodied `eq()` helper defined at `:138`. Counted on the pin: **17** `eq(...)` call sites in `[138-158]`, and the run prints `17 cases pass.` — so the number is **accurate today**. That is the whole of the defect: nothing derives it and nothing compares it, so it is accurate by coincidence and stays accurate only until the next case is added or removed.

Same class as #15231 (`check-wildcard-fallthrough`, 17 printed / 18 asserted) and #15291 (`check-skill-compatibility-version`, 7 printed / 6 declared) — both of which are the same construct **after** it went stale. This one is the pre-stale state of the identical shape, which is why it is worth taking now rather than after it drifts.

## Why it is not merely cosmetic

`checklist-select.mjs` has no assertion floor (the #13799 census reads it NONE), so the printed count is the only quantity a reader has. A count that shrinks silently with the array — or, here, one that does not move at all when the array does — is exactly the "a battery that never ran is indistinguishable from one that passed" reading #13799 exists for. It also mis-serves the floor work directly: a floor is set from a measured count, and the number printed here is not a measurement.

## The remedy

Derive it, as the sibling files already do. `scripts/check-i18n-walk-parity.mjs:527-536` and `scripts/render-release-coverage-anchor.mjs:159-166` both keep a counter incremented inside the assertion helper and interpolate it, and `check-i18n-walk-parity` states the rule in place:

> Counted, never transcribed: a hand-typed case count in the success line is a number that goes stale the first time a case is added, and a self-test whose own report is wrong is the last place to keep one.

So: a `cases` counter incremented as the first statement of `eq()`, and `${cases}` in the success line. Roughly four lines, no assertion semantics touched.

⚠️ Changing the green line moves the byte-comparison that #13799's batches use to prove a floor transplant is inert, so this is cleanest either **before** `checklist-select.mjs` is floored or **in the same PR that floors it** — not in between.

## Scope note

Filed unassigned from the #13799 batch-8 census (measurement only, no edits). Not repaired there: out of that batch's scope, and the file is a floor candidate whose batch has not been dispatched yet.
